review.comment: You show the right idea for displayName: trim then collapse spaces with split/join. The badge string uses $var instead of ${var} so values never interpolate, handle logic throws on String.split, and level or empty-name checks are absent. Next: return [L${level}] name (@handle) via template literals, normalize handle to lowercase without @, and throw the README errors.

Name and handle normalization are on the right track and you fixed template literal interpolation. The level check cannot parse: close the parenthesis and use Number.isFinite(rawLevel) with Number.isInteger for level >= 1. Your if/else conditions are reversed and return ERROR strings instead of throw new Error per the README. Next: throw invalid level and displayName is required with corrected guards.

Display name and handle normalization are solid, and the happy-path badge matches the README examples with template literals. Level validation still uses rawLevel.isFinite instead of Number.isFinite and Number.isInteger, so level 0 is not rejected. Errors return strings instead of throw new Error with the exact README messages. Next: fix the level guard and throw invalid level and displayName is required.

Display name and handle normalization are correct and happy-path badges match the README examples with template literals. Errors still return strings instead of throw new Error with the exact README messages, and level 0 passes validation because the check omits level >= 1. Next: add rawLevel < 1 to the guard and throw Error with messages invalid level and displayName is required.

Display name and handle normalization are correct and happy-path badges match the README examples with template literals. Throwing on errors is the right direction, but messages use an ERROR prefix instead of the exact strings invalid level and displayName is required, and level 0 still passes because the guard omits level >= 1. Next: add rawLevel < 1 to the level check and throw new Error with the exact README messages.

Pass (100): Display name and handle normalization match the README examples, including trim, space collapse, lowercase, and @ stripping. Error paths throw the exact messages invalid level and displayName is required. Template literals build the badge correctly. Solid match to all acceptance criteria.
